chats.answer:
For a USB-C MacBook Air, I’d buy the UGREEN Nexode 20,000mAh 130W. It has enough USB-C power to charge the Air quickly while you use it, and it can charge your phone at the same time. If you only need to charge the laptop, though, a 65W power bank is usually sufficient.

Best picks

UGREEN Nexode 20,000mAh 130W

Best overall

UGREEN US

100W from the main USB-C port, plus up to 30W for a phone. Useful power display; weighs 476g. The 130W rating is combined output, not laptop charging speed. 
UGREEN US

65W to a single device is a good match for an Air. The attached cable saves you carrying another one; less charging headroom than the UGREEN.

100W through the attached USB-C cable and up to 80W input to refill the bank. Slightly bulkier than the Anker.

How much charge will 20,000mAh give you?

A 20,000mAh laptop power bank stores roughly 72Wh, but conversion losses mean less reaches the MacBook’s battery. As a practical estimate, with the laptop asleep:

MacBook Air

	

Expected added charge




13-inch M1

	

90–110%




13-inch M2 or newer

	

85–105%




15-inch

	

70–85%

These are estimates, not measured results for your MacBook. Charging while working will leave you with a smaller battery-percentage gain.

Bottom line: Get the standard UGREEN if prices are similar. Choose the Anker if you prefer a flatter design and built-in cable. I assumed you have a USB-C-capable Air and prioritized charging performance over minimum weight; your exact model and budget could change the pick.

chats.answer:
For a MacBook Air, I’d look for a 20,000mAh power bank with at least 65W USB-C Power Delivery output from a single port. That’s enough for comfortable everyday charging on modern Air models; 70W or more gives you fast-charging headroom on supported models.

My pick: the UGREEN Nexode 20,000mAh 130W. It has more than enough output for an Air, can charge a phone alongside it, and earned a positive review from Macworld. 
Macworld

100W main USB-C port, separate 30W USB-C port, 72Wh capacity and a useful power display. The drawback is its chunky, 476g body. 
UGREEN US

If you carry your Air in a slim laptop sleeve, I'd consider this instead:

Baseus Blade HD 20,000mAh 100W

$83.48

Walmart - Baseus · 4.4/5 (25 reviews)

A flat, roughly 20mm-thick design that fits better beside a laptop. Its 100W output is still ample for an Air.

How much battery will you get? Budget for roughly one full charge of a 13-inch Air, or around 70–90% of a 15-inch Air, with the laptop asleep. These are estimates, not model-specific test results; conversion losses and using the Mac while charging reduce the gain.

I'd buy the UGREEN unless the flat shape matters to you. I assumed you have a USB-C-chargeable Air (2018 or newer) and prioritized value over minimum weight. Your exact model could change the charging-speed and capacity estimates.
